rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Plug points + UX
rules_evaluated.evidence: Plug points (44a) are well-named and structurally invited (student's own repo, own backlog task, sponsor-stated rules home). But 44b UX fails: the body claims 'one question at a time' four separate times (L7 'What you build', L59 pre-action lead-in, L67 'Answer the branches...', L109 'What happened' recap), while the actual fenced prompt push-back-on-the-plan-2.md batches 'three at a time' three separate times ('Walk down every unresolved branch of the design tree three at a time', 'Ask me three questions at a time', 'I'll confirm or correct three at a time'). A fast operator reading prompt-to-prompt hits a 'wait, what?' count mismatch between what the body promises and what the pasted prompt actually requests.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Reconcile the body's 'one question at a time' framing (L7, L59, L67, L109) with the fence's actual 'three at a time' batching in push-back-on-the-plan-2.md, in whichever direction is the intended design.
